title: Browse Agent Tool Manifest
description: Declares a tool the agent may call. Built-in tools, WASM plugins and external MCP servers all use this manifest so PolicyEngine can treat them uniformly (ADR-005, ADR-008).

name.description: Stable identifier exposed to the model, e.g. `click`, `github_create_issue`.

description.description: Model-facing description. Treated as trusted only for built-in tools; plugin descriptions are shown to the user at install.

runtime.description: Where the tool executes. `mcp_stdio` requires explicit user installation and is per-task enabled.

entrypoint.description: Path to .wasm component or MCP command line. Absent for builtin.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the arguments object. Each property may carry `x-browse` annotations (see $defs/argumentAnnotation).

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity class assigned to the tool's output when it re-enters the model context.

untrusted_content.description: If true, output is labelled as untrusted data (like page content). Mirrors WebMCP `untrustedContentHint`.

capabilities.description: Least-privilege capabilities the tool needs. The runtime denies anything not listed. Shown to the user at install/enable time.

read_only.description: Tool has no side effects on the page, device or network state. Enables auto-allow within scope.

consequential.description: Tool performs a real-world / irreversible action (pay, send, delete, publish, upload). Always requires user confirmation with preview (ADR-005 §6). Mirrors WebMCP `consequentialHint`.

consequential_when.description: Optional deterministic predicates that make an otherwise neutral tool consequential, e.g. `click` on a submit button in a form with payment fields.

requires_dev_mode.description: Only available when the user has enabled dev mode (e.g. localhost access, browser-mcp).

preview_template.description: Template for the confirmation preview, e.g. `Click "{{target.name}}" on {{target.origin}}`.

kind.description: `ref`/`obs_id`/`mem_id` are references into runtime-owned data (provenance is then known exactly). `free_text` is model-authored text and is only accepted where `free_text_ok` is true.

free_text_ok.description: Whether model-authored free text may be passed. Fields like passwords or payment numbers must never set this.

allowed_provenance.description: Provenance labels accepted without confirmation. `origin_other` (data read on another origin) always triggers a cross-origin flow confirmation unless a grant exists (ADR-005 §3).

secret_forbidden.description: Values labelled `secret` are rejected before the model ever sees them.
